D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Four named tools are listed by the Claude directory; no annotations were publicly displayed there. AgentDiscoverability reproduces guidance attributing all four as read-only, but endpoint annotations were not observed. 2. No server-enforced confirmation flow was established; the surfaced instructions recommend asking/displaying clarifying questions in some search flows. 3. OAuth resource metadata names 11 scopes, including three order-write/read scopes; inheritance from product roles, admin controls, allowlists, redirect approval, token expiry, and revocation behavior beyond the published revocation URL are unknown. 4. No read-only endpoint, filters, toolsets, modes, or sandbox endpoints found. Third-party guide says US-only; Thumbtack's official announcement describes the integration as for US users. 5. Tool descriptions expose business/review data and ZIP-based queries; no MCP-specific masking or PII exclusion documented. 6. Third-party guidance describes search results and a review limit parameter (max 20); no MCP quota/rate limit observed. 7. Guide-derived parameter instructions include US ZIP validation and mapping form answer IDs; server-side validation/correction was not observed. 8. MCP logging, auditing, telemetry, and opt-out were not found. Thumbtack's general privacy policy describes platform communications monitoring and data uses, but does not specify MCP calls. 9. No feedback/rating/report/survey tool is in the four listed names or descriptions. General connector copy steers users toward matching with pros; no separate marketing elicitation identified. 10. No server-delivered skills tool found. Assistant-facing behavior rules appear in third-party-reproduced descriptions; enforcement by the server is unknown. 11. Third-party guide describes search IDs and filtering an existing search; persistence and expiration semantics are not independently observed. 12. One global hosted endpoint is evidenced; no hierarchy or sub-server disclosed. 13. No raw API, arbitrary request, SQL, script, or execute tool appears in the four-tool inventory. Resource scopes include order operations without corresponding named tools in the public list.

E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Thumbtack's general Partner Platform documents marketplace APIs for submitting project requests and APIs for user accounts; its pro integrations cover leads, messages, profiles, and customer activity. F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Third-party pages reproduce guide instructions to use ZIP codes explicitly, preserve result ordering, limit review display, and present specific result messages. These are agent-facing instructions; the available evidence does not show server enforcement.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Thumbtack's privacy policy says it collects and uses platform information, may use AI tools to process information and train internal systems, and may disclose information with consent or for platform operation. It does not specify MCP-specific collection, retention, or model-training treatment.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Thumbtack's announcement describes a native experience for US Claude users to find local pros and continue to Thumbtack to connect and hire. The Claude listing says users can browse recommendations and connect with a pro.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: General privacy and product claims are not linked to MCP-specific enforcement in available sources. Search and review-display rules are documented as agent-facing guidance in third-party reproductions; server enforcement was not observed. The OAuth metadata indicates authorization protection, while some third-party listings incorrectly describe access as authless.

contradictions: The supplied OAuth resource metadata lists 11 demand scopes, including demand::orders.write and order read scopes, while the public Claude directory lists only four read-oriented search, category, and review tools. The additional scopes do not establish additional MCP tools.

The endpoint returned HTTP 401 and publishes OAuth protected-resource metadata, but Claude's directory labels sign-in as not required; Tedix and Manufact also describe open/no-auth access despite reporting OAuth requirements or failed authentication checks.
MCP.so reports no tools detected, while Claude's directory, Tedix, Manufact, and Agent Discoverability each report the same four tool names.
observations_for_research: OAuth scopes advertise broader order-related access than the named tools available in public listings, creating a distinction between authorization capability and discoverable tool surface.
The listed workflow tools include assistant-facing sequencing and display instructions, including result-order preservation and constraints on how returned business data is rendered.
